drafts.headline: Backlog forecasts run about 33% too low for TMGH.
drafts.plain: The method misses this driver in the same direction almost every time, not at random. That is a fixable defect rather than noise — find what is wired wrong before adding any correction factor.
drafts.evidence: Bias -0.284 log (about 33% too low), average miss 0.441, wrong in the same direction in 71% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=35).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A later run of the same name where the sign no longer holds across bootstrap blocks.
drafts.declined: an arithmetic consequence of the new-sales miss, not an independent finding: the order book rolls forward as prior book plus sales less revenue, so a low sales forecast produces a low book by construction

drafts.headline: A depreciation forecast built on a projected asset base cannot see an acquisition.
drafts.plain: Depreciation is usually projected as a rate on a fixed-asset balance the model has also projected. That works until the company buys something. An acquisition multiplies the asset base overnight and the forecast has no way to know, so the error is not noise — it is the deal.
drafts.evidence: Bias -0.253 log (about 29% too low), average miss 0.435, wrong in the same direction in 80% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=30).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A name with no acquisition inside the tested window whose depreciation forecast still misses in the same direction and by the same size.

drafts.headline: A developer's work in progress runs ahead of its revenue, not with it.
drafts.plain: Half-built homes are an investment made years before the revenue they produce. Driving work in progress off revenue makes the model spend when the company has already spent, and it will understate the balance every time the company is building for a growing order book.
drafts.evidence: Bias -0.528 log (about 1.7 times too low), average miss 0.528, wrong in the same direction in 100% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=25).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A developer whose work in progress tracks its revenue closely over a full cycle.
drafts.applies_to: real-estate developer, off-plan, point-in-time on handover

drafts.headline: A reported finance charge is not always interest on borrowings.
drafts.plain: Before dividing a finance charge by debt to get a borrowing rate, check that the charge is actually interest on that debt. Where a company recognises a financing component on its customer contracts, the reported charge includes something no lender is being paid, and the implied rate is not a rate at all.
drafts.evidence: Bias -1.224 log (about 3.4 times too low), average miss 1.224, wrong in the same direction in 100% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=30).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: An issuer whose finance-cost note splits interest on borrowings from every other financing charge, where the implied rate then matches its disclosed borrowing cost.

drafts.headline: The size of a demographic anchor's miss on a developer is set by the launch calendar, not by the method.
drafts.plain: A population-based volume driver runs low for every developer, but not by a fixed amount. How far low depends entirely on what the company launched, which means the miss cannot be corrected with a multiplier fitted on one name and carried to another.
drafts.evidence: Bias -0.877 log (about 2.4 times too low), average miss 1.022, wrong in the same direction in 76% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=33).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A third developer whose miss lands close to one of the first two, which would suggest a stable offset after all.
drafts.applies_to: real-estate developer, off-plan, point-in-time on handover

drafts.headline: For a balance-sheet stock, assuming no change is a strong benchmark.
drafts.plain: Stocks move slowly. A model that forecasts one has to beat simply carrying last year's balance forward, and it often does not. Check that explicitly before presenting a projected balance as if it added information.
drafts.evidence: Negative skill against the freeze benchmark at horizons 1, 2, 3, 5, worst -0.555.
drafts.why_scope: Losing to a naive benchmark usually points at the method, which would make it ALL — but confirm it is not this company's series being unusually persistent.
drafts.overturned_by: A stock series volatile enough that carrying it forward is clearly worse than modelling it, at most horizons.

drafts.headline: The finance cost forecast loses to assuming no change.
drafts.plain: At 5 of 5 horizons, simply carrying last year's number forward beat the model. A method that cannot beat 'no change' has not earned the precision it displays, and should be published as a range or not at all.
drafts.evidence: Negative skill against the freeze benchmark at horizons 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, worst -0.363.
drafts.why_scope: Losing to a naive benchmark usually points at the method, which would make it ALL — but confirm it is not this company's series being unusually persistent.
drafts.overturned_by: A later run where the model beats the freeze benchmark at a majority of horizons.
drafts.declined: the same finding as the finance-cost lesson registered from this run — the driver loses to no change because its numerator and denominator describe different things, which is recorded there rather than twice

drafts.headline: The customer advances error is the company, not the currency.
drafts.plain: Re-running every forecast with perfect foresight of inflation barely improves it. So devaluation is not the explanation, and looking for a macro fix would waste the effort.
drafts.evidence: Average miss 0.627 as known, 0.687 with perfect foresight of inflation — the macro share is only -9.6%.
drafts.why_scope: Almost always ALL — 'check whether the macro explains it before assuming it does' is a method rule — but the specific finding may be about this market.
drafts.overturned_by: A market or period where the same decomposition puts most of the error on the macro path.
drafts.declined: a NEGATIVE macro share on eleven observations is noise, not a finding: it says perfect foresight of inflation made the forecast slightly worse, which cannot be a real property of the decomposition

drafts.headline: Perfect foresight of inflation removes almost none of a forecast error, even across a devaluation.
drafts.plain: It is tempting to blame a bad forecast on the currency. Re-run every forecast knowing the inflation path in advance and see how much improves. Usually almost nothing does, which means the error is in how the business was modelled and looking for a macro fix wastes the effort.
drafts.evidence: Average miss 0.677 as known, 0.623 with perfect foresight of inflation — the macro share is only 8.1%.
drafts.why_scope: Almost always ALL — 'check whether the macro explains it before assuming it does' is a method rule — but the specific finding may be about this market.
drafts.overturned_by: A market or period where the same re-run removes most of the error.

drafts.evidence: Average miss 0.808 as known, 0.775 with perfect foresight of inflation — the macro share is only 4.1%.
drafts.why_scope: Almost always ALL — 'check whether the macro explains it before assuming it does' is a method rule — but the specific finding may be about this market.
drafts.overturned_by: A market or period where the same decomposition puts most of the error on the macro path.
drafts.declined: subsumed by the net-profit finding registered from this run: the same measurement on a smaller driver, and filing it separately would count one observation twice

drafts.headline: The customer advances bias changes direction between regimes.
drafts.plain: It runs one way in one period and the other way in the next. Averaging them produces a correction that is wrong in both. Record it, do not correct for it.
drafts.evidence: By era: E2 post-float +0.597; E3 devaluation -0.211.
drafts.why_scope: A sign that flips with the regime is usually about the market or the period, not the company — but say which.
drafts.overturned_by: A longer record in which one sign dominates across all regimes.
drafts.declined: one of five drivers showing the same regime instability in this run; the pattern is registered once, from the overheads draft, rather than five times

drafts.headline: In a high-inflation market, a driver bias that changes direction between regimes is the normal case, not the exception.
drafts.plain: A bias measured over a whole history can hide two opposite halves, and in a market with several currency regimes that is what usually happens. Split the record by regime before treating any measured bias as a fact — on this company a third of the drivers changed sign.
drafts.evidence: By era: E2 post-float +0.325; E3 devaluation -0.169.
drafts.why_scope: A sign that flips with the regime is usually about the market or the period, not the company — but say which.
drafts.overturned_by: A market or period where fewer than one driver in ten changes sign between regimes.
